Both of these targets are ultimately linked to SNB-78, indicating a possible pathway where 2,3,24-Trihydroxy-12-ursen-28-oic acid may influence the activity of these kinases, which in turn could modulate SNB-78 function. The scores from the two paths suggest a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, with the first path showing slightly higher confidence (0.5301) compared to the second (0.5231). The evidence supports a mechanistic link between the compound and SNB-78, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated. The presence of multiple targets along this pathway highlights the complexity of the relationship and underscores the need for further experimental validation to confirm the proposed mechanism.
